B) Offers multiple pathways to achieve your own and others' current and future professional
development needs.
C) Intellectual impairments
D) Physical environment adjustments
3. Which of these is NOT considered a form of reasonable adjustment?
A) Consideration on the candidate's language, literacy, numeric capability
B) Adjustment to the physical environment or venue
C) Offering materials in alternate formats
D) Read printed information and give the answer to the candidate.
4. Which of the following is the most appropriate assessment method for individuals with low literacy or
numeracy skills?
A) Written multiple-choice test
B) Online questionnaire
C) Oral questioning and verbal responses
D) Essay writing task
5. Why is it important to examine our perceptions to promote inclusivity?
A) It helps maintain personal biases.
B) It is an important starting point in promoting an inclusive learning environment.
C) It has no impact on creating an inclusive environment for the TVET learner.
D) It helps to identify the trainer selection.
6. Which of the following is considered preventive maintenance?
A) Adjusting, and routine replacement
B) Fixing a broken part
C) Replacing a part after a breakdown
D) Ignoring small faults
Page 2
7. Which of the following describes corrective maintenance?
A) Maintenance actions conducted to keep equipment operational.
B) Inspection and adjustment to prevent equipment from malfunctioning.
C) Repairing equipment only after a problem has occurred.
D) Replacement of equipment based on age, not condition.
8. What should be done with damaged or unsafe equipment?
A) Immediately report the issue and isolate the equipment from use
B) Proceed with use until a replacement is available
C) Relocate it to another area to avoid detection
D) Dispose of or sell the equipment without informing others
9. What is the purpose of shadow boards in workshops?
A) To randomly store tools
B) To visually organize and track tool usage
C) To store tools in safe environment
D) To replace traditional shelves for store tools in good condition
10. Why is it important to conduct regular inspections of training facilities?
A) To reduce training hours for to ensure safety
B) To minimize documentation work
C) To ensure safety and functionality
D) To promote trainer comfort only

Part C: Short Question Answers
1. What is inclusivity? Why practice inclusivity?
Answer: Inclusivity means recognizing, accommodating and meeting the learning needs of all your
learners. It means acknowledging that your learners have a range of individual learning needs and are
members of diverse communities. Inclusivity means making sure everyone feels welcome, valued, and
respected, no matter who they are or where they come from.
By fostering and promoting an inclusive learning culture, training and/or assessment organization can:
Prepare its learners to work more effectively and flexibly in diverse workplaces and communities
Page 6
Provide more learners and clients with better quality services in an increasingly competitive market
Ensure it meets its obligations arising out of legislation and standard
2. What principles should be integrated into work practices to foster an inclusive learning culture?
Answer: In order to foster and promote an inclusive learning culture, you must integrate the principles
that underpin inclusivity into all of your work practices, and these principles include:
using learner-centred approaches to learning;
fostering and advocating independence;
supporting equal opportunity for participation;
creating opportunities for participation and success;
ensuring cooperative approaches to learning;
supporting, encouraging and valuing individual contributions;
acknowledging current strengths and skills as a basis for further learning;
motivating learners through change; and
making reasonable adjustments to procedures, activities and assessment for equity.
3. What do you understand by 'clients with particular needs'?
Answer: It is also important to acknowledge, respect and value clients with particular needs, including:
Women where under represented
People with low literacy, numeracy
People with disability
Rural and remote learners
Youth at risk
4. Who are some support persons that may assist in inclusive learning? Give examples and their roles.
Answer: Support persons assist learners to overcome barriers and participate fully in training and
assessment.
Examples and Roles:
Teacher Aides / Learning Support Officers: 1. Help learners with disabilities during training or
assessments. 2. Provide one-on-one guidance or assist with equipment.
Interpreters / Translators: 1. Assist learners with limited English proficiency or hearing impairment. 2.
Translate instructions, questions, or responses.
Counsellors / Student Advisors: 1. Provide emotional, social, or career support. 2. Help learners manage
stress or personal issues affecting learning.
Mentors / Peer Support: 1. Guide learners through tasks or practical activities. 2. Encourage
participation and build confidence.
Family Members / Carers (where appropriate): 1. Assist with mobility, communication, or personal care
needs during training.
5. How will you monitor and improve inclusive work practices?
Answer: Having promoted a culture of learning within your training and/or assessment organisation,
you now need to monitor and improve your own work practices, and this will involve:
identifying, modifying and improving your work practices to enhance inclusivity;
reviewing strategies and policies to support inclusivity; and
documenting and reporting policy changes.
6. What is maintenance?
Answer: Maintenance is performing the routine actions which keep the device in working order, to keep
in good condition, to preserve and protect the device.
7. What is the difference between Preventive Maintenance and Corrective Maintenance?
Answer: Meaning: Preventive - Planned maintenance done before a fault occurs; Corrective -
Maintenance done after a fault or breakdown occurs
Page 7
Purpose: Preventive - To prevent breakdown and extend equipment life; Corrective - To repair the fault
and restore the equipment to working condition
Timing: Preventive - Scheduled / regular (daily, weekly, monthly); Corrective - Unscheduled, when a
failure happens
Examples: Preventive - Cleaning, oiling, adjusting, routine replacement of parts; Corrective - Fixing a
broken part, replacing a part after breakdown
Cost / downtime: Preventive - Lower cost, less downtime; Corrective - Higher cost, more downtime
8. Write down 5’S Approach in Workshop Keeping?
Answer: 5S is a Japanese workplace-organisation approach used to keep the workshop clean, safe and
efficient:
1. Sort (Seiri) – remove unnecessary items from the work area.
2. Set in order (Seiton) – a place for everything and everything in its place.
3. Shine (Seiso) – clean the workplace and equipment regularly.
4. Standardize (Seiketsu) – set standards and procedures for the first three S.
5. Sustain (Shitsuke) – make 5S a habit through discipline and regular checking.
9. What are the steps involved in maintaining training equipment and tools?
Answer: Maintaining training equipment and tools is essential for safety, efficiency, and longevity. Here
are the key steps involved:
Regular Inspection.
Cleaning.
Proper Storage.
Preventive Maintenance.
Repair and Replacement.
Documentation.
Training and Awareness.
10. Explain how maintaining facilities contributes to creating a positive image for an organization?
Answer: Maintaining facilities contributes to creating a positive image for an organization by:
Ensuring SAFE environment
Improving MORALE of human resources
Reducing operational COST
Increasing PRODUCTION
Prolonging LIFE facilities
Prompting delivery of services and products
Ensure it meets its obligations arising out of legislation and standard
